target_customer: Digital nomads, remote workers and remote-first companies that need health insurance outside their home country
problem: Remote workers and freelancers abroad lacked affordable health coverage; traditional plans were tied to a country or expensive.
business_model: Subscription insurance (Nomad Insurance, later Nomad Health) underwritten by partner insurers, sold direct online without brokers
product_category: Insurtech: global health and travel insurance for remote workers

founders.name: Sondre Rasch
previous_startups: Superside (formerly Konstant; co-founder and CEO, YC W16)
founders.background_notes: Age as stated in TechCrunch, March 2018.

founders.name: Sarah Sandnes
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch spells her name Sarah Beyahte Sandnes; age as stated March 2018.

investors: Norwegian Investment Authority (as written by TechCrunch)

technical_complexity.rationale: A subscription web product with coverage underwritten by an established insurer (Tokio Marine's Worldtrips per later sources); the hard parts were regulatory and claims operations, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Pricing without brokers and a focused nomad niche, but coverage is underwritten by partner insurers, so rivals could copy the offer; no network effects or lock-in documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source names an incumbent that copied or bought the offer. The company later launched Nomad Health (Nov 2023) and Nomad Citizen (2025 beta) and states 2,000+ companies served in 175+ countries.

market_need_then: At launch in March 2018 TechCrunch reported a $37 monthly plan for foreigners living abroad; the founders were themselves digital nomads and the idea came from freelancers at Superside lacking affordable health insurance.

branding.name_origin: Rasch told TechCrunch (March 2018) the name fits the company's focus on freedom and safety. A search summary of the same article also attributes a migrating-birds rationale; not confirmed on a direct read.
branding.domain_note: Operates on safetywing.com (exact .com); acquisition history not found.

identity.mascot_or_character: Illustrated bird waving a passport (image file named Milo); the site does not call it a mascot
identity.visual_style: Playful hand-drawn illustrations of clouds, squirrel, bush, ship and city lights
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, warm, light humor ('It's just a bush.')

branding.brand_signature: Illustrated bird-with-passport character and the 'global safety net' mission
branding.community_and_virality: Nomad 101 webinars, the Borderless newsletter, SafetyWing Stories, Nomad Care Map and an Ambassador program; reviews on nomad blogs. Claims of 12,000-member Plumia community are unverified.

brand_strength.rationale: A coherent playful identity and a mission narrative with many nomad-blog reviews, but no source quantifies brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: SafetyWing grew from a sub-$500K angel round in March 2018 to a $35M Series B in April 2022 on a subscription health plan for remote workers, helped by the rise of remote work. A founder interview cited by Latka puts revenue near $24M in April 2023 versus about $12M a year earlier. It is still independent and expanding into Nomad Health and a membership product; the main risks are underwriting dependence and regulation, and revenue figures are unaudited estimates.
notes: Series B lead differs by source (Kinnevik vs Mundi Ventures) and total raised is quoted at $46-47M. A $195M post-money valuation for the Series B appeared in one search summary without a clear source and is not recorded. Latka revenue figures ($12M 2021, $24M Apr 2023, $34.1M Oct 2024) are founder-interview or estimate based. The 2018 TechCrunch article names no competitors and no other dated source was found, so the competitor list is empty. Ages are those stated in that article. Web Archive skipped.
